Blast radius: validate_arr_url has exactly one production caller, triggarr/web/routes.py:522 (the settings-form save path). It is not called when config loads or when the daemon starts, so URLs already saved in config are not re-validated. Running instances cannot fail on startup after upgrading.
Public API: the signature (url: str) -> tuple[bool, str] and the error string 'Blocked address' are unchanged. Callers need no changes.

Regression check: the only newly rejected inputs are multicast addresses (224.0.0.0/4, ff00::/8) and IPv4-mapped forms of loopback, link-local, unspecified and multicast addresses. None of these can host a Radarr or Sonarr HTTP API, so no supported value is newly refused. The tests at tests/test_validation.py:128-133 confirm that mapped private LAN addresses (::ffff:192.168.1.100, ::ffff:10.0.0.1) are still accepted, which keeps the documented intent of allowing private networks.

On Python 3.13+, IPv6Address.is_loopback and related checks already look through ipv4_mapped addresses, so the new branch is redundant there but harmless. On 3.11 and 3.12, which the project floor allows, the branch is required. Either way the behavior is correct on every supported version.
No schema, migration or persistence impact. Performance is negligible: a few constant-time checks run on a form submit.
Verdict: shippable as-is. The remaining denylist gaps (NAT64/6to4, decimal-integer hosts, trailing-dot hostnames) are pre-existing and filed as a low-severity note.
